h1: Khanom Golden Beach Hotel — a beachfront stay on Nai Phlao Beach you can walk straight onto
intro: If you're heading to Khanom for the pink dolphins and want a hotel where opening the balcony means the sea is right there, Khanom Golden Beach Hotel nails the location — it sits right on Nai Phlao Beach, just steps from the sand, and every room has a sea-view balcony. It's a 3-star hotel of around 60 rooms with a beachfront pool, a kids' pool, a fitness center and a beachside restaurant, and the breakfast draws praise for its choice. From approx. ฿1,200/night.

body.html: Khanom Golden Beach Hotel sits right on Nai Phlao Beach (sometimes called Nai Dan Beach) in Khanom District, Nakhon Si Thammarat. Its selling point is obvious — the beachfront location. You walk a few steps from the hotel straight onto the sand, and every room has a sea-view balcony. It's a seven-storey building, and the upper floors take in a wide sweep of beach, sea and distant mountains, which is the view guests photograph most.

The hotel has around 60 rooms across several types — Superior, Hollywood Twin and Deluxe. Rooms feel spacious for the price, with air-conditioning, a TV, a small fridge, tea and coffee, and bathrooms with a shower (some with a tub). In reviews, what guests praise most is the balcony sea view, the room size and the cleanliness. The building and some fittings show their age, though — this is not a brand-new hotel, and it's worth going in knowing that.
"Opened the curtains in the morning and the whole balcony was sea. Walked down for a swim right in front of the hotel — easy. The staff were lovely and really helpful too."

The pool sits right by the beach, looking out to the water, with a separate kids' pool — handy for families who want both a pool and the sea in one place. There's a ground-floor gym, Thai massage, a games room and a beachside restaurant serving Thai, Chinese and European dishes. Breakfast is mentioned warmly in many reviews for its choice, but during quieter periods the hotel switches from buffet to an à-la-carte, order-per-dish format, which is good to know up front.

Things to know before you book. Honest reviews flag the ageing building and fittings — hot water can be weak in some rooms, power outlets are few, and some air-con units and TVs are old with a poor TV signal. The beach in front is more about the view than the postcard-white sand of bigger resort beaches, and there can be plenty of insects at night by the sea, so keep the balcony door shut. Priced against newer resorts in Khanom it's broadly comparable, so it's worth comparing a few before you decide.

On location, Khanom is known for its pink dolphins and quiet beaches that haven't gone the way of Samui or Phangan. From the hotel it's a short drive to the dolphin-watching pier and sights like Ao Thong Nod, Khao Plai Dam and the Phap Pha stone bridge. It's about a 10-minute drive from Khanom Bus Station and roughly two hours from Nakhon Si Thammarat city. Public transport is thin around here, so a car or rental is the easiest way to get around.

To be straight about it, Khanom Golden Beach Hotel is not a sleek new luxury resort — its appeal is the beachfront location, the walk-straight-onto-the-sand convenience, a sea view from every room, a beachside pool and an accessible price for a beachfront stay. It suits families and couples visiting Khanom for a relaxed beach break who aren't expecting five-star polish. If you can live with an older building and you're here mainly for the sea view, the value works. If you want a brand-new room with modern fittings throughout, consider a newer resort in Khanom instead.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for a high floor facing the sea directly for the widest, best view. On long weekends and in high season Khanom gets busy, so book ahead. If you're here for the pink dolphins, take a morning boat when the sea is calmer and sightings are more likely — the hotel can help arrange a boat in advance.

faqTitle: FAQ — Khanom Golden Beach Hotel, Khanom

faq.q: Is Khanom Golden Beach Hotel really right on the beach?
faq.a: Yes. The hotel sits on Nai Phlao Beach (Nai Dan Beach), just steps from the sand, and every room has a sea-view balcony. Upper floors take in a wide view of beach, sea and distant mountains — it's the property's main draw.

faq.q: How much does Khanom Golden Beach Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿1,200/night for a Superior Sea View room. There are also Hollywood Twin and larger Deluxe rooms on higher floors with wider views. Prices rise on long weekends and in high season, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is this hotel good for families?
faq.a: Very much so. It has a beachfront pool and a separate kids' pool, direct beach access for a swim, spacious rooms and free parking — ideal for families who want both a pool and the sea in one place while visiting Khanom.

faq.q: What is breakfast like at Khanom Golden Beach Hotel?
faq.a: Breakfast is praised for its good choice. During quieter periods, though, the hotel may switch from a buffet to an à-la-carte, order-per-dish format. If breakfast matters to you, check the format with the hotel in advance.

faq.q: How do I see the pink dolphins and explore Khanom from here?
faq.a: Khanom is famous for its pink dolphins. The dolphin-watching pier is about a 15–20 minute drive, and sights like Khao Plai Dam, the Phap Pha stone bridge and Ao Thong Nod are 20–30 minutes away. Public transport is limited, so a car or rental is best.

faq.q: What should I know before booking?
faq.a: Go in knowing it's a long-established hotel where the building and some fittings show their age — hot water can be weak in some rooms, outlets are few, and TV signal can be poor; there are also insects at night by the sea, so keep the balcony door shut. The appeal is the sea view and beachfront location, not new-build polish.
